extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, administrative officials, tribunal registrars, and lawyers dealing with Canada Pension Plan and Unemployment Insurance appeals and overpayment recovery
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural standards and requirements governing notifications, filing, internal distribution, recovery of overpayments, sanctions, and appeals (rulings, Minister determinations, referrals, and Umpire appeals) under the Canada Pension Plan and the Unemployment Insurance Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of notification of decision to appellant
rubrics_metrics.description: A form letter accompanies the notification of decision and, if the decision was unfavourable to the appellant, he is advised of his right to appeal to the PAB (provided authorized by the Chairman). The letter informs the claimant that he must lodge his appeal within 90 days, a period that may be extended on request by the PAB, and indicates the address of the Registrar to whom all communications are to be directed. A copy of Rules of procedure of the PAB (CPP Benefits) is enclosed with the secretary's letter. If the decision is in the appellant's favour, the form letter notifies him that the Minister has the right to appeal to the PAB on the same conditions, and that the Registrar of the PAB will inform him in the event of the Minister's decision to avail himself of this right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure form letters state: (1) whether decision is favourable or unfavourable, (2) 90-day appeal period and extension possibility, (3) Registrar address for communications, and (4) enclosure of relevant Rules of Procedure; if favourable, inform about Minister's right to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate internal distribution of Review Committee decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General is informed of the Review Committee's decision immediately (the director of the district bureau can transmit it by word of mouth to the Appeals Section). The physician or lawyer who acted as the Minister's representative also receives a copy of the decision from the secretary, as well as all the documents that were introduced in evidence before the Committee by the appellant. Finally, the secretary forwards to the Appeals Section a complete file, together with a report in which he summarizes the appellant's allegations and arguments at the hearing and provides, if applicable, the names of his representative and his witnesses. It is on the basis of this file and report, as well as of the recommendation made by the Minister's representative before the Committee, that the Director General may have to decide whether to lodge an appeal to the PAB or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative practice: distribute decision copies promptly to Director General, Minister's representatives, and forward a summarized file/report to Appeals Section to inform any decision to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission to Registrar of PAB within 48 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary transmits to the Registrar, by registered mail and within 48 hours of the decision, a complete file made up of the appeal files provided to members of the Review Committee prior to the hearing, the originals of all documents tabled before the Committee by both litigants, the original of the decision, and the signed undertaking of the Committee members to keep the matter of the hearing secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and send a complete registered file to the PAB Registrar within 48 hours including: appeal files given to Committee members, originals of documents tabled, original decision, and signed secrecy undertakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation to prepare transcript or minutes of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the regulations nor custom oblige the secretary to prepare any [transcript or minutes]. The notes that he takes in the course of the hearing serve only to assist the Committee in its deliberations on the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect formal transcripts/minutes as a standard; secretary's notes are for internal use only unless otherwise required.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90-day time limit to lodge appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The letter informs the claimant that he must lodge his appeal within 90 days, a period that may be extended on request by the PAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals should be filed within 90 days of communication of the decision; note procedures for requesting an extension from the PAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical delays for Review Committee appeals — expect several months
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of cases appealed to the Review Committee should take several months. In the sample, the average time that elapsed between the rendering of a decision on the appeal to the Minister and the decision of the Review Committee amounted to 276 days; for disability-related claims it was 296 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrators and appellants should anticipate multi-month timelines (often 6–10 months) between Minister-level decisions and Review Committee hearings/decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 65: immediate repayment obligation for overpayments
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 65 of the CPP obliges any beneficiary that has received or cashed a cheque to which he was not entitled, or the amount of which exceeded the sum that he was entitled to receive, to return the cheque or to reimburse the issuer to the amount of the excess payment immediately. Failing to do so, he renders himself liable to civil prosecution in the Federal Court, in recovery of the excess amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients who receive overpayments must return/repay immediately or risk civil recovery; however correspondence inviting contact to negotiate repayment is standard practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiated repayment and instalment arrangements (practical practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The form letter addressed to the recipient of an overpayment to claim reimbursement invites him to get in touch with the district office and negotiate terms for repaying the excess amount, if he finds that a lump sum settlement of the matter would cause him financial hardship. The CPP Administration is entirely willing to conclude arrangements for repayment by instalments and historically has not had to resort to legal action to effect recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District offices should offer and negotiate instalment repayment plans and avoid litigation where possible; communicate willingness to accommodate financial hardship in the notification letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recoupment under Section 505: apportionment of recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 505 of the Canada Pension Plan Regulations authorizes the Director General, 'having regard to all the circumstances of the case', to apportion the recovery of overpayments over a period of time that he considers reasonable. In practice, the district office director will be authorized to negotiate with the debtor the amount to be deducted from each benefit cheque still payable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recoupment (deductions from future benefits) where the debtor remains or becomes eligible; apportion recovery reasonably and negotiate deduction amounts via district office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial remission/waiver of overpayment recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister has the option of waiving in whole or in part his right of recovery against the beneficiary when the debt appears to be practically irrecoverable, or the sum to be recovered is insufficient to justify the expenses inherent in effecting recovery, or again, and above all, when recovery would result in 'undue hardship' for the debtor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider recommending remission where recovery is impracticable, uneconomic, or would cause undue hardship; district office staff should assess financial situation and recommend remission to the Minister.

rubrics_metrics.name: No remission where overpayment due to deliberate fraud (section 92)
rubrics_metrics.description: The remission of the debt may not be authorized in cases where the overpayment was due to the deliberately fraudulent conduct of the beneficiary, a conduct which renders him liable to criminal sanctions under section 92.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate intent; if overpayment arose from deliberate fraud, remission is not appropriate and criminal sanctions may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal offences for false or misleading statements and overpayment-related conduct (section 92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 92 contemplates false or misleading statements (either by commission or omission) made with the deliberate purpose of obtaining benefits, the cashing of a cheque representing a benefit payment to which one is not entitled, and the deliberate failure of the recipient of an overpayment to send back the cheque or to reimburse the Department to the sum of the overpayment. The element of intent is an essential ingredient of these offences, except for the cashing of a cheque representing an overpayment (a curious exception).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecutions for fraudulent obtaining or retention of benefits require proof of intent (except for cashing an overpayment cheque). Consider criminal referral only where deliberate conduct is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode and limitation period for prosecuting offences
rubrics_metrics.description: The offences must be prosecuted by way of summary conviction within five years of the commission of the offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of the five-year limitation and summary conviction procedure when assessing criminal prosecution options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized disclosure offence by officials (section 107(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: The deliberate disclosure by an official of information concerning an individual, obtained for CPP purposes, to a person having no legal right to the information is covered by section 107(7). This offence renders the offender liable to prosecution by way of summary conviction within five years of the commission of the offence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect beneficiary confidentiality; unauthorized disclosure by officials may lead to summary conviction within five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ruling procedure characteristics (coverage/rulings officer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ruling: comparatively informal, not authorized by any specific provision. Involves an initial decision rendered at the local level or by the Coverage and Interpretations Section. The Rulings Officer may demand the employer provide information by means of a questionnaire to which the latter must respond; refusal renders him liable to a fine. The procedure provides for consultation of the two parties concerned by the Officer. No reason is assigned for the decision, although the parties are informed of their right to ask for a determination by the Minister on the question at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulings are informal, can be initiated by worker/employer/inspector, may require compliance with information questionnaires (fines for refusal), and do not usually include reasons; parties should be told about right to seek a Minister's determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination by the Minister: procedure and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination: structured by the Act; may be made either at the request of the employer or employee, or at the initiative of the Department. The procedure calls for the notification of third parties likely to be affected by the Minister's decision. The Minister is required to afford an opportunity to all parties concerned to submit observations in writing. Officials of the Determinations and Appeals Section take into account PAB caselaw and the Umpire's caselaw in drafting the determination. Notice of the determination is transmitted to the parties in the same way as in the case of CPP-related determinations. No reason for the determination is given, though the notification indicates the possibility of appeal to the Umpire, under section 84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking or issuing a Minister's determination, notify affected third parties, solicit written observations, consider tribunal caselaw, and include appeal information even if reasons are not provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the Minister (hierarchical review of assessments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal to the Minister provided under both Acts is a recourse for hierarchical review of an assessment directing an employer to pay contributions and to deduct and retain his employee's contribution from the latter's salary. The appeal may focus on whether the worker is an employee subject to the Act or on the amount for which he has been assessed. Notification informing the parties of the decision draws their attention to their right to appeal, on the one hand, to the PAB (as regards their CPP contribution) and, on the other, to the Umpire (as regards their unemployment insurance contribution). It invites them to communicate with the Registrars of the respective administrative tribunals, indicating the address of each and specifying the time limit within which an appeal may be lodged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appeal notifications clearly specify tribunal(s) for CPP and UI aspects, provide Registrar contact details, and state applicable time limits for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral on an application for benefits (section 75(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 75(3) provides for a procedure analogous to that of the determination or appeal, but begun at the initiative of the Employment and Immigration Commission. Questions must arise in consequence of an application for unemployment-insurance benefits and must concern exclusively the determination of whether the occupation of the worker is subject to the plan. Officials in the Commission district office draw up a request enumerating relevant information and transmit it to a Rulings Officer. If further information is necessary, the Officer contacts the parties directly. The Officer transmits his decision, without assigning reasons, to the Commission which then rules on the application for benefits. If the Commission rejects the application on the ground that the claimant's occupation does not come within the scope of the Act, the claimant has 90 days to challenge this ruling by asking the Minister for a determination. If the Commission accepts the applicant, the employer has the right to contest the ruling and ask the Minister for a determination. The Commission may not always inform the claimant and employer of these avenues. Referral procedure can give rise to unjust dealing where a claimant receives benefits in good faith later found to be ineligible and is required to repay; the Umpire has urged the Commission to waive recovery on humanitarian grounds where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making or receiving referrals: document the factual basis, inform parties of appeal rights and 90-day challenge periods, and consider humanitarian waiver recommendations where a Commission error causes claimant hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Umpire's powers on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Umpire may rule on any question of fact or law whose solution is necessary to the settlement of the litigation, and he may, of his own authority, vacate or vary the challenged decision. His decision-making power is effectively no less broad than that of the Minister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the Umpire has broad remedial powers (fact and law) and can substitute his own decision in place of the administrative decision under appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal requirements to the Umpire (form and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle the notice of appeal must be filed with the Registrar in accordance with the form prescribed under section 4 of the Rules of Procedure. It must contain a presentation of the facts in the case and the grounds on which the appellant relies in his appeal; it must specify the date of the challenged decision as well as the date on which it was communicated to the appellant (so the Registrar can verify whether the 90-day time limit has been respected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare notices of appeal using prescribed form: include factual presentation, grounds, date of challenged decision and date of communication. However expect liberal interpretation and possible dispensation of strict formality by the Umpire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Umpire's discretion to relax formalities and extensions (section 26 and section 84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 26 of the Rules of Procedure allows the Umpire to dispense appellants from strict adherence to prescribed form, a power he has made considerable use of. Section 84 provides for the possibility of securing an extension of the time limit for filing an appeal, so long as the application for the extension is made within the time limit. The Umpire usually rules on the request in the light of the appellant's written observations, without a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants of limited means may rely on Umpire discretion for form and time extensions; file extension applications within the time limit and submit written observations for the Umpire's consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical accessibility and communication of appeal process
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrasing of departmental form letters formerly invited parties simply to 'communicate' with the Umpire's office, causing confusion and making many appellants believe the Umpire was one more level of the administration rather than an administrative tribunal. This ambiguity required that the Registrar be liberal in interpreting what constituted a notice of appeal. Formalities surrounding initiation of an appeal are sufficient to cause many appellants to withdraw or seek legal advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft communication to appellants clearly to avoid misunderstanding (explicitly identify Umpire as tribunal, provide form and Registrar info). Be ready to apply liberal interpretations to notices from unrepresented appellants to avoid unfair dismissal of appeals.
